title: Economic Sanctions as Collective Punishment: The Case of Venezuela
publisher_or_archive: Center for Economic and Policy Research (CEPR), Washington D.C.
summary: Pioneering econometric and epidemiological study evaluating the human cost of US unilateral financial and petroleum sanctions against Venezuela, finding that sanctions fit the legal definition of collective punishment under international conventions and caused an estimated 40,000+ excess civilian deaths in 2017–2018 by depriving the country of essential foreign currency to import medicine, food, and water treatment supplies.
